history.period: 9th century CE (initial shrine); present structure 13th-14th century CE
history.summary: Siddhapeeth/Shaktipeeth dedicated to Raj Rajeshwari Bhagwati at Dokahar Sthan near Baharwan Belahi village (Madhepur panchayat), Kaluahi block, on the bank of the Chandrabhaga river. Legend: the goddess appeared in the dream of priest Pandit Rupi Upadhyaya of Mahrail village and directed him to recover her idol from the river; the idol, said to be over 1100 years old, was installed on the riverbank. The present Tirhut-style temple was built by Mahesh Thakur of the Raj Darbhanga in the 13th-14th century CE. An undeciphered ancient inscription (Shilalekha) stands at the sanctum entrance; archaeologists have begun efforts to read it. Locally called 'Tirth Raj'. CSV DISTRICT/TOWN CORRECTION: listed as Darbhanga - the temple is actually in Madhubani district (Kaluahi), about 35 km from Darbhanga city; the Darbhanga link is via its builder, the Raj Darbhanga. Coordinates from the 'Maa Raj Rajeshwari Asthan, Kaluahi' location listing; reverse-geocoding confirms Dokahar, Kaluahi.
